transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2028-10-11 09:00 PDT | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jared (Atlas SRE), Maya (Atlas CTO), Rohan (Atlas Engineer)

Auto-generated Summary: brief demo of tracing and request logs, focus on debugging production failures and instrumenting alerts.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we got about 45ish minutes, we'll run through the console tracing experience then dive into request logs and a couple debugging flows. Priya will do the demo, I'll cover pricing/next steps.
[00:14] Maya: great, thanks Alex, quick note we're primarily concerned about production errors hitting our chat assistant. Latency and PHI handling are big flags for us.
[00:28] Alex: totally understood, we'll call out encryption, KMS, VPC options. Priya over to you.
[00:32] Priya: ok jumping into the console, so here is the tracing tab, um, you'll see the timeline view, this is per-request trace, uh, we capture SDK request-id, model route, and hardware node. sometimes the transcription will show node names a bit odd like g-pu-2b instead of gpunode-2 but, uh, we map it back in metadata.
[01:05] Rohan: can you filter on a specific user id or request id? we've had trouble correlating logs to our SRE traces.
[01:15] Priya: yes, there's a filter at top, you can paste request-id, session id, or route, and it highlights traces. i'll paste one your SRE found earlier, quick demo. (screen share)
[01:42] Priya: ok so this trace shows the full timeline: client -> edge -> auth -> model call -> post-process. you can expand spans, see per-span latency and the backtrace to a specific GPU allocation. the KV cache hit is shown as a green tick in the model span.
[02:18] Jared: that KV cache bit - is that prefix cache or full KV cache? we saw weird cache invalidations last week.
[02:29] Priya: good question - we show both. in the trace details it says cache_type: prefix | kv and cache_hit: true/false. sometimes the transcription or label says kv cash, sorry for that, but the value is accurate.
[03:00] Priya: next, the error analysis page. this aggregates errors across requests and groups them by signature, stack, and route. here's an example where an upstream audio decode lib caused a spike - you can click the group to see sample requests and full request logs.
[03:25] Maya: how long do request logs live in hosted by default? we need 90 days for audits sometimes.
[03:33] Alex: hosted default is 30 days, we offer add-on retention to 90 or 365 days depending on plan; Dedicated/Private you control retention and can ship to your S3.
[03:46] Rohan: and encryption at rest - we use a customer-managed key.
[03:50] Priya: yes we integrate with KMS/HSM, you can bring-your-own-key for Dedicated and Private; for hosted there's an option to use CMK for enterprise tier.
[04:10] Priya: now drilling into a failing request, i filter by request-id and open the request log. you can see headers, prompt, policy checks, model response, and the internal stack. notice the model response says timeout at 3s, but the overall trace shows 3.2s, so you can see where the tail latency happened.
[04:42] Jared: are those request logs searchable by metadata? like route, model, region?
[04:48] Priya: yes searchable and taggable. we also support exporting a subset as ndjson for post-hoc analysis, e.g., you can export all timeout requests from the last 24 hours.
[05:05] [crosstalk] Maya: and retention for those exports?
[05:09] Alex: exports are up to whatever you store downstream - we push to your S3 or you can download.
[05:18] Priya: switching to the flame/timeline view - you can see nested spans, CPU/GPU times, and a heatmap for retries. this helps distinguish model time vs infra time. often customers assume model is slow but it's actually in the network auth layer.
[05:45] Rohan: could we attach our tracer ids? we use OpenTelemetry across our stack.
[05:51] Priya: yep we ingest OpenTelemetry trace ids if you forward them; we have a mapping so you can jump from your trace to Redwood request. that mapping is included in the SDK headers or via our proxy.
[06:12] Alex: quick pause - these integrations are important for your SRE workflow and for incident post-mortems.
[06:20] Priya: next is the replay/debug tool - you can replay a request in a sandbox environment, change model variant, or toggle kv cache to see diffs. here i replay a failed request and toggle quantization to show a regression.
[06:46] Maya: can replays run against our private deployment? we don't want production data leaving VPC.
[06:52] Priya: yes for Private or Dedicated inside your VPC the replay happens within your network; for hosted we provide a redacted replay mode or customer-controlled replay where the payload never leaves your region.
[07:12] Alex: also worth noting audit logs and RBAC - every replay is logged and tied to user identity (SSO).
[07:20] Rohan: speaking of SSO, does Redwood support SAML and SCIM provisioning?
[07:26] Priya: yes SAML, OIDC, and SCIM for user sync in enterprise plans. the console has RBAC roles pre-baked: viewer/operator/admin and custom roles.
[07:40] [00:07:40] Jared: on the performance side, you mentioned batching and autoscaling - can we see how batching changed latency?
[07:50] Priya: in the Optimize tab we surface batching metrics and a recommended batch size per route. you can run an A/B where 50% of traffic goes through a batcher to validate. here's a sample chart showing p95 drop from 220ms to 150ms with small batching.
[08:15] Maya: ok latency targets - we often need p95 under 150ms for web experiences. does Redwood guarantee that?
[08:23] Alex: guarantees are part of Dedicated SLA. Hosted typically has best-effort but we have performance profiles and we architect for low-latency. For firm SLAs we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[08:35] Priya: also you can pin model versions and have automatic fallback to a smaller, faster variant on high load. this shows in the trace as a fallback span.
[08:50] Rohan: how do we set alerts for error spikes?
[08:55] Priya: console has alerting tied to traces and error groups - thresholds on error rate, p95, and we support webhook/Slack/Syslog destinations. we also send enriched payloads with sample request-id and a trace link.
[09:10] Maya: one of our blockers is data residency - EU requests must stay in EU.
[09:16] Alex: we have region routing and can route by policy so EU traffic stays in eu-west region, and for Private you can host entirely in your region.
[09:30] Priya: moving on, showing the request logs table - you can pivot by route, model, user_id, status. there's a 'show related traces' link which surfaces all traces with the same session id.
[09:51] Jared: sometimes our logs show partial prompts - does the console store full prompts?
[09:57] Priya: by default we redact PII and sensitive fields in hosted mode; you can opt into full prompt storage in enterprise with appropriate agreements. in Dedicated/Private it's under your control.
[10:12] Rohan: what about token-level cost breakdown in traces? we want to attribute cost per endpoint.
[10:17] Priya: we show token counts and estimated cost per request in the trace and post-aggregation reports by route/model, that's part of the Optimize feature.
[10:30] Alex: quick interjection - we'll include the cost breakdown demo spreadsheet in the follow-up.
[10:35] Priya: demo - here's a real debug scenario: a sudden spike of 500 errors for route /chat-infer. i click the error group, see top stack is a protobuf decode error in upstream library. i open a sample request, then open the linked trace which shows the model responded fine but our post-processing crashed.
[11:05] Maya: that's similar to our incident - we saw successes but the post-process had a null pointer. this would help.
[11:12] Priya: then you can assign the error group to a team and add a note, export the sample requests to a csv for your engineers.
[11:22] Rohan: can we recreate the same environment for testing? e.g., same model weights and quantization?
[11:28] Priya: yes for Dedicated/Private you can snapshot model variant and quant settings; for hosted we allow model variant pins and provide a dev sandbox with the same weights for parity.
[11:42] Alex: any questions about procurement/security while Priya wraps the demo?
[11:48] Maya: yes - SOC2 and pen test reports?
[11:51] Alex: we will share SOC2 Type II and recent penetration test summary; full reports under NDA. also we support customer-managed KMS, private link/VPC endpoints and audit logs.
[12:05] Priya: finishing up with request-log replay - here's an example where i re-run the request against the same model but with increased timeout and the trace now shows success. you can see before/after side-by-side.
[12:28] Jared: does replay hit your production infra?
[12:31] Priya: replays are sandboxed, unless you explicitly choose to run in prod for non-hosted deployments. for hosted we spin up an ephemeral environment and log everything.
[12:47] Rohan: curious about network routing - if we go Dedicated with reserved capacity, can we pin to certain AZs?
[12:54] Alex: yes Dedicated capacity has region and AZ affinity options and predictable throughput; you can configure autoscaling and burst policies.
[13:05] Priya: last bit - how to onboard quickly: we have SDKs, a quickstart, and a data collection script to stream request logs to Redwood. we'll share a runbook.
[13:20] Maya: what's typical pilot length?
[13:22] Alex: pilots are commonly 2-4 weeks; goal is to validate latency/cost and a small set of production traces. we can scope a 2-week pilot to focus on the chat assistant.
[13:32] Priya: i'll note that onboarding includes setting up SSO, RBAC, and a sample retention policy.
[13:40] Jared: for our SREs, can we get an API to pull traces programmatically?
[13:45] Priya: yes all data is available through API; we have an endpoints to query traces, request logs, and exports. rate-limited of course but fine for automation.
[13:58] Maya: any concerns with PHI? we need HIPAA controls - audit trails and BAAs.
[14:05] Alex: we support HIPAA customers on Private deployments with BAAs. Hosted can be configured but typically Private is the path for PHI due to network controls.
[14:20] [14:20] Rohan: ok how about cost, what does Dedicated cost look like roughly?
[14:27] Alex: rough ranges - depends on reserved GPU class, but we'll send pricing tiers; for small pilots we often start with a modest reserved pool plus overage for burst.
[14:40] Priya: walking through the final console items - drilldowns, alerts, and the debug flow where we linked a trace to an error group and scheduled a runbook item.
[15:00] Maya: this is helpful; what I'd like for next steps is a pilot with sample logs and a success criteria doc.
[15:07] Alex: agreed. i'll send the template and a proposed pilot SOW.
[15:12] Priya: i'll provision a trial tenant and upload a sanitized log sample for you to try the dashboard. you'll get admin access for the SREs.
[15:22] Jared: will that include replay capability?
[15:25] Priya: yes, replay in sandbox and the ability to replay in your VPC if you choose Private.
[15:33] Maya: timeline - can we start next week?
[15:36] Alex: yes we'll aim to have trial tenant by Friday, 2028-10-13.
[15:42] [crosstalk] Rohan: last technical q: do you capture model kv cache diagnostics like hit/miss ratio per route?
[15:50] Priya: yes hit/miss ratios are visible in Optimize and traces; you can group by time window and route. we also recommend quantization settings per workload.
[16:10] Alex: ok, recap of actions - Alex will send pilot template, pricing, and SOC2 docs; Priya will spin up tenant and upload sample logs; Atlas will provide failing request ids and confirm pilot success metrics.
[16:26] Maya: perfect. thanks everyone.
[16:30] Alex: thank you, we'll follow up over email and set the pilot kickoff.
[16:36] Priya: thanks all, reaching out to schedule the kickoff.
[16:40] Meeting end.
